course_aims: This course provide students with experiential learning in research through the conduct of a chosen research project and workshops. Students will lead the development and analysis of primary research in the field of Dentistry. Students will employ effective scientific communication skills through the writing of a scientific manuscript and communicating their findings to experts in research.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply ethical considerations underpinning research in a health project.
Critically evaluate, transform, and interpret information in the context of the existing knowledge base and translational implications of the findings.
Demonstrate effective academic writing in the production of a research report suitable for publication in a peer-reviewed journal.
Discuss and justify the research methods, and conclusions in defence of the research findings.
Interpret and transmit research findings to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Develop and demonstrate the teamwork capabilities required to collaboratively construct a rigorous research project.

assessment_details.task_description: This assessment stream consists of three progress interviews designed to support and monitor the development of the research project. Conducted at key points across the course, these tasks provide opportunities for feedback on project governance, individual and group engagement, and overall progress. The first group task focuses on ethical governance and data collection status. The second task is an individual interview to assess each student’s understanding and contribution to the project. The final group interview evaluates project advancement and readiness for completion. These tasks aim to assist with project management, support successful completion of the research project and ensure individual accountability for the project. assessment_details.other_conditions: Student specific, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: Students will deliver an oral presentation summarising their research project. The presentation should clearly outline the background and rationale for the study, including justification for the chosen study design and methods. Students should then present the results, interpret and discuss their findings, and provide clear conclusions and implications arising from the project. Students should also highlight and reflect on their contribution to the research project. Following the presentation, students will be asked questions to clarify aspects of the work and demonstrate their understanding of the study design, methods, results, and conclusions. Performance parameters, and assessment criteria and standards will be made available on the course Blackboard site prior to the assessment. The presentation will be recorded and retained as per university policy. The recording will be stored in a secure manner and will only be accessed if required for the purposes of moderation of marking; provision of feedback to the student; and/or re-marking following a successful re-mark application. learning_activities.topic: Research (Self Directed) Students undertake an independent research project under the guidance and supervision of academic staff. Through regular meetings and feedback, students develop their research and subsequently prepare a written research report that presents their methods, findings, and conclusions. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05, L06
